value.first: Now's the window. The method is iron-first solids with early-and-often allergen introduction. Day 1: sit him fully upright in a high chair, calm moment, rested and a little hungry, and offer a spoon or two of one iron-rich food - iron-fortified oat cereal mixed with your milk or formula, pureed well-cooked beef, or mashed lentils. Most ends up on the tray. That's a win.
value.second: Days 2-7: build to iron-rich food twice a day, add mashed veg and fruit. Milk continues as usual - solids add to it. Week 2, peanut: in the morning thin half a teaspoon of smooth peanut butter into warm water or a puree (never a glob, never whole nuts), small taste, wait 10 minutes, then the rest, and stay with him two hours. No other new foods that day. Next day or the one after: well-cooked egg, same routine.
value.third: Then one new allergen a day - yogurt or cheese, wheat, tofu, sesame, thinned nut butters, fish - and once tolerated keep each in about twice a week, because dropping it can undo the protection. Waiting doesn't protect: early peanut cut allergy about 80% in the LEAP trial. Gagging is noisy and normal; choking is silent. If he has moderate-to-severe eczema, talk to your provider before allergens. I'll check in Thursday.
